blocks.body:
## Technical summary

The measured Donkey Kong Country bottleneck is the legacy Unity tile **presentation path**, not SNES CPU/APU execution. Stock v0.300 held **59.98 emulated frames/s** while consuming **2.99 process CPU cores**. The DKC framebuffer renderer reduced process CPU to **1.61 cores**; exact retained backgrounds reduced it to **1.30 cores** while preserving **60.01 emulated frames/s**.

The production-relevant implementation is `SuperZSNESDKCFramebufferRendererIL2CPP`: a supported-frame final compositor, renderer-owned retained background planes, and strict raster-effect partial-row refresh. `SuperZSNESPerformanceSuiteIL2CPP` contains independent scheduler-correctness and service controls. `SuperZSNESNativeAtlasDirtyFixIL2CPP` is a reusable native-patch reference whose measured performance effect was neutral.

## Renderer replacement changes the CPU envelope

The supported framebuffer path reduced end-to-end process CPU **46.0%** versus stock. Retained backgrounds extended the reduction to **56.5%**. The result carries a memory trade: the retained configuration's endpoint working set was about **107 MiB higher** than stock.

## Repository implementations and their boundaries

The table maps each retained enhancement to the exact repository project, measured status, principal downside, and the portion of the design that remains useful in a later source-level implementation. The atlas reference is intentionally outside this production list because its current benchmark result is neutral.

## `SuperZSNESDKCFramebufferRendererIL2CPP`

### Supported-frame compositor

The mod reconstructs supported DKC Mode 1 BG, OBJ, priority, window, brightness, and color-math output into a persistent final framebuffer. One texture upload replaces repeated Unity tile-mesh and material construction. Unsupported frames fail closed to the stock renderer.

**Downsides.** It is DKC- and feature-profile-specific rather than a complete general SNES PPU renderer. Unsupported modes and effects regain the legacy renderer's CPU cost, so fallback bursts can still produce scene-specific stalls. PPU accuracy becomes the new compositor's responsibility. The implementation also consumes more memory and is pinned to the audited 32-bit v0.300 binary.

**Reusable architecture.** A per-frame capability gate preserves correctness while feature coverage expands. The final framebuffer is a clean ownership boundary: cached planes cannot be overwritten by stock Unity mesh pools. Bounded fallback telemetry records unsupported reasons without adding synchronous per-frame file I/O.

## Renderer-owned retained backgrounds

The cache hit **79.1%** of eligible per-layer decisions in the measured scene. Background preparation fell from **1.933 to 0.976 ms (-49.5%)**, and process CPU fell another **19.5%** versus framebuffer cache-off.

**Downsides.** Exact state snapshots and retained planes contribute to memory use. Conservative invalidation produces misses; incomplete invalidation risks stale pixels. Continuous scrolling or palette/VRAM changes naturally reduce hit rate.

**Reusable architecture.** Cache resources are owned by the replacement renderer. Input snapshots are committed only after a successful complete build, and all relevant PPU state participates in invalidation.

## Strict partial rows remove the recurring BG2 rebuild

DKC's line-81 BG2 scroll effect previously rebuilt all 224 rows every four frames. Redrawing only changed-scroll rows reduced background work **63.9%**, complete framebuffer work **16.2%**, and average Unity Update time **11.9%**. The path was used for **700 of 715** raster-effect rebuilds per accepted trial.

**Downsides.** It applies only when relevant VRAM is byte-identical and BGSC, BGMODE, and character-base state are unchanged. Every other change takes the full path. Dirty-region support increases state-tracking and oracle-test requirements.

**Reusable architecture.** Dirty regions derive from semantic PPU changes. Optimized and complete paths share the same pixel representation, allowing exact fixture comparison and full-rebuild recovery for every ambiguous state.

## `SuperZSNESPerformanceSuiteIL2CPP`

### Bounded scheduler-backlog accounting

Stock `MasterExecutor.Update` can execute at most five owed frames and then subtract every owed frame, permanently discarding the excess. The mod restores only the proven normal-speed backlog and drains it through later stock-sized batches; fast-forward arithmetic remains unchanged.

**Downsides.** This restores timeline correctness rather than reducing work. Catch-up can temporarily raise CPU demand, and presentation still occurs once per Unity Update. Recovered intermediate emulated frames are therefore not guaranteed to appear. In one controlled pair, emulated cadence improved while presentation cadence fell.

**Reusable architecture.** `due`, `executed`, and retained debt are separate quantities. Only executed work is charged, debt is bounded, and emulation cadence is measured separately from presentation cadence.

### History and rewind service guards

The same mod can suppress history screenshot and rewind work only during `Update`, then restore the exact user values. This prevents known synchronous service work but has no measured steady-state throughput gain. The corresponding history or rewind feature is not populated during a guarded interval. Native persistent settings are the simpler implementation when available.

## `SuperZSNESNativeAtlasDirtyFixIL2CPP` is a reference pattern, not a measured win

The stock 2/4/8-bpp accessors mark atlas pages dirty before testing whether a tile changed. A managed Harmony experiment counted about **1.26 million false page hits** per trial but increased presentation work **37.1%** by adding a callback to every tile access.

The native reference moves six page-dirty assignments onto the existing true-dirty branches with zero managed hot callbacks. Four trials per configuration measured **2.6249 ms stock versus 2.6356 ms fixed presentation (+0.41%)** and **1.2350 versus 1.2234 process CPU cores (-0.94%)**. Both movements were inside run-to-run noise, so the patch remains disabled.

**Reusable architecture.** Hot-path changes belong at the source/native branch rather than behind per-call managed detours. The plugin demonstrates full-binary and expected-byte gates, failure-safe patch ordering, partial rollback, unload restoration, and leaving the on-disk binary unchanged.

## Stock-renderer source changes retained for future versions

The Mono/v0.230 projects below are not ABI-compatible with v0.300. Their source-level changes remain useful wherever the general Unity tile renderer is retained for other games, Mode 7, menus, or framebuffer fallback frames.

**`SuperZSNESMaterialCacheGuard`.** `tileAddrToMat` grew from 253 to 210,853 historical keys in about 35 seconds and retained more than 1.2 million list slots. Per-background scratch lifetime plus high-water list pooling kept the live map at 0-42 keys; allocations plateaued at 1,308 across more than nine million rentals. A periodic map clear was rejected because it caused 100-195 ms stalls.

**`SuperZSNESMeshBoundsOptimization`.** Conservative fixed bounds replace per-upload `RecalculateBounds()` for viewport-clipped 2D meshes. One moving-window comparison improved presentation 2.65% and reduced two-frame batches from 169 to 111. Broad bounds weaken culling in unusual multi-camera/editor scenes; mesh-notification batching regressed and remains disabled.

**`SuperZSNESRendererFastPaths`.** Verified `TryGetValue` and `HashSet.Add` source cleanups remove redundant probes in ordinary, Mode 7, cleanup, and dynamic-font paths. The evidence does not isolate a causal gain for this mod alone, and supported framebuffer frames bypass the ordinary path.

**`SuperZSNESPerformanceGuard`.** Optional rewind/history work and unnecessary 4x internal surfaces can be avoided. Later sessions observed roughly 110 MiB lower working memory with services off and 2x surfaces. The feature loss is explicit; VSync/90/120/240 Hz experiments are not retained as general fixes.

## Correctness and instrumentation bugs fixed

The repository also contains verified correctness and compatibility fixes. These are listed independently so a source-level cleanup is not mistaken for a measured throughput gain.

## Integration facts

- The measured performance configuration is `SuperZSNESDKCFramebufferRendererIL2CPP` with retained backgrounds and automatic strict partial-row refresh.
- Scheduler recovery is an independent optional correctness change, not part of the renderer speedup.
- History and rewind guards are independent service controls.
- The managed atlas gate is rejected. The native atlas implementation remains disabled and serves as a verified reference.
- Older dictionary, material, mesh, draw-loop, and stock-background-cache mods target paths bypassed on supported framebuffer frames and are not part of the v0.300 implementation set.
- `Assembly-CSharp.dll` and `GameAssembly.dll` remain unchanged on disk. Runtime patches are exact-version gated and native bytes are restored on unload where applicable.

## Evidence scope and limitations

- Ordinary configurations used two fresh processes, 12 seconds of warmup, and approximately 20-21 seconds of measurement with VSync at 1.
- Partial-row results used two fresh 60-second trials per configuration.
- Native atlas results used four fresh processes per configuration.
- The workload is one difficult DKC gameplay scene. Fades, menus, Mode 7, unsupported-state fallback rate, and a full playthrough were not characterized by the same dataset.
- Process CPU includes emulation, Unity, audio, presentation, and diagnostics.
- Memory values are endpoint samples, not long-run plateau measurements.
- The renderer effects are large and replicated. Sub-1% movements are not treated as established gains.

implementationMap.reuse: Semantic dirty regions with exact full-build equivalence and recovery

implementationMap.downside: Catch-up work; recovered frames are not necessarily presented

implementationMap.downside: History/rewind data is not populated while guarded
